assertions.title: Newsletter included in EML file generation

steps.action: Expand Newsletter card, set heading to 'Store Updates', type body text with bold formatting
steps.observed: Editor shows 'Store Updates' heading and bold body text

steps.action: Fill required Date Range field to enable preview/download
steps.expected: Preview and download buttons become enabled
steps.observed: Preview shows email content, Download Email Draft button enabled

steps.action: Click 'Download Email Draft' button and capture EML content via blob interceptor
steps.expected: EML file generated with newsletter section
steps.observed: EML content captured (10019 chars) with complete newsletter section

steps.expected: Proper MIME headers, CRLF line endings, multipart structure
steps.observed: MIME-Version: 1.0, Content-Type: multipart/alternative with boundary, Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable, CRLF line endings confirmed

steps.action: Verify newsletter section in HTML part of EML
steps.expected: Newsletter HTML with inline styles at configured position
steps.observed: Newsletter section found in HTML part with inline styles (background-color, border-left, font-size, color). Position: TOP (newsletter before BRAND SECTIONS, before HOW TO SHOP). Rich text formatting preserved (<strong> tags for bold).

steps.action: Expand Newsletter card and fill heading 'Store Updates'
Type body text 'Welcome to our store! We have exciting updates for you this month.' and apply bold formatting
steps.observed: Editor shows text with bold formatting applied

steps.action: Check preview panel shows newsletter section
steps.expected: Newsletter visible in email preview at correct position
steps.observed: Preview shows 'Store Updates' heading and body content in email layout, positioned before brand section

steps.action: Download EML file via 'Download Email Draft' button
steps.observed: EML content captured via blob interceptor (10019 chars)

steps.action: Inspect EML HTML part for newsletter content
steps.expected: Newsletter section with heading, body, and inline styles at correct position
steps.observed: HTML part contains: <!-- NEWSLETTER --> comment, 'Store Updates' heading with inline styles (font-size: 18px, color: #1e40af), body with <strong> tags, inline container styles (background-color: #f9fafb, border-left: 4px solid #2563eb). Newsletter positioned before BRAND SECTIONS (top position).

assertions.title: Position toggle changes placement in preview

steps.action: Verify default position is 'Top' (Top button has data-active='true')
steps.observed: Top button has data-active='true', Bottom button has no data-active

steps.action: Check preview HTML shows newsletter before BRAND SECTIONS (top position)
steps.expected: NEWSLETTER comment before BRAND SECTIONS comment in HTML
steps.observed: NEWSLETTER at position 717, BRAND SECTIONS at 1282, PROMO LINE at 1435 - newsletter correctly before brand content

steps.expected: Bottom button becomes active, Top button deactivates
steps.observed: Bottom button data-active='true', Top button data-active=null

steps.action: Check preview HTML shows newsletter after BRAND SECTIONS (bottom position)
steps.expected: NEWSLETTER comment after BRAND SECTIONS comment in HTML
steps.observed: BRAND SECTIONS at 717, PROMO LINE at 870, NEWSLETTER at 915 - newsletter correctly after brand content and before HOW TO SHOP (1486)

steps.action: Click 'Position: Top' button to toggle back
steps.observed: Top button data-active='true', Bottom button data-active=null

steps.action: Verify preview returns to top position

frictions.description: Position toggle buttons use aria-label attributes ('Position: Top', 'Position: Bottom') rather than visible text labels in the accessibility tree, making them harder to discover via standard snapshot. Had to use semantic locators (find role button --name) to interact with them.
frictions.resolution: Used agent-browser find role button click --name 'Position: Top' and 'Position: Bottom' to interact with the toggle buttons.

frictions.description: agent-browser --download-path option cannot be changed mid-session when the daemon is already running. Had to use a JavaScript blob interceptor to capture EML content instead of downloading to a specific path.
frictions.resolution: Installed a Blob constructor interceptor in the browser to capture the EML content when the download button was clicked, then extracted it via eval.

summary: Tested 3 assertions: all passed. VAL-EMAIL-009: EML file contains newsletter section at configured position with inline styles and RFC 5322/2045 compliant headers. VAL-CROSS-001: Full compose→preview→export workflow verified end-to-end with rich text preservation. VAL-CROSS-002: Position toggle correctly moves newsletter between top (before brand sections) and bottom (after brand sections, before HOW TO SHOP) in the preview.
